title: Fewshot robustness squashpad
content:
Goal: quick living scratchpad for small experiments that try to make few-shot exemplar sets robust to distribution drift, token budget limits, and format hallucination. Not polished; lots of TODOs and short-hand.

Quick context:
- Working with hosted-api and dedicated variants. Seen brittle outputs when small label distribution shifts happen (e.g., class names change, new abbreviations).
- Want a lightweight protocol for curating 3-8 exemplar sets that generalize across prompt framing changes.

Hypotheses to try:
1) Interleaving negative examples (explicitly labelled "bad answer") reduces hallucination on novel classes.
2) Anchor-shot pattern (first shot = canonical mapping table) stabilizes output labels.
3) Mix of 1-shot + 5-shot (combo templates) yields best tradeoff for 512 token budget.

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Model variants: rwd-3b-q4, rwd-7b, rwd-13b-ffnopt
- Temp: 0.0, 0.2, 0.6
- Shots: 1, 3, 5, anchor+2
- Prefix styles: instruction-only | roleplay | schema-first
- Inputs: clean (in-distribution), noisy (abbrev + typos), novel-labels (introduced new category names)

Example exemplar set (3-shot anchor style):
--PROMPT--
You are an assistant that maps product short descriptions to canonical taxonomy tags. Use exactly one tag from the allowed list: [analytics, security, infra, ux, payments]. If unsure, say "unknown".

Anchor: mapping rules: treat "auth" as security; "latency" as infra; abbreviations: "UX" -> ux.

E1:
Text: "SAML integration for single sign-on"
Tag: security

E2:
Text: "db replication lag and monitoring"
Tag: infra

E3:
Text: "credit card payout flow"
Tag: payments
--END PROMPT--

Failure cases observed so far:
- Model invents composite tag like "security-infra" instead of single allowed tag when prompt is long or token budget small. (rwd-7b temp 0.6, 3-shot)
- When allowed list capitalized (e.g., [Analytics, UX...]) model returns lowercase mixed forms. Inconsistent casing breaks downstream strict parsers.
- Abbreviation drift: new team uses "authn"/"authz"; exemplar had only "auth" mapping and model outputs unknown.
- Negative examples sometimes lead to over-conservative "unknown" outputs. Need balance.

Quick mitigation ideas (to test):
- Enforce schema by appending "Return EXACTLY ONE of: analytics|security|infra|ux|payments|unknown" on its own line at end of prompt (hard constraint).
- Post-filter: simple regex map to collapse multi-word tags to first matching allowed token. Useful for short-term.
- Shot diversity: include at least one example with novel short form (authn/authz) to improve recall during test.
- Casing normalization: instruct: "Return tag in lower-case exactly as in list".

Evaluation plan (fast):
- Small held-out set: 300 examples across in/noisy/novel labels. Metric: exact-match rate, hallucination rate (output token not in allowed set), downstream parser failures.
- Track per-model latency and avg token cost (hosted pricing).

Short-running experiments to run next (priority):
1) rwd-3b-q4 anchor+2 vs 3-shot non-anchor, temp 0.0 -> check hallucination rate. (ticket INF-4321)
2) rwd-7b with enforced schema trailing line vs without, 5-shot noisy input set.
3) Post-filter pipeline prototype: simple deterministic mapper + fallback to model output; measure recall loss.

Notes / heuristics from quick trials:
- Trailing exact-match line reduces hallucination but increases unknowns if examples ambiguous. Might need 1 clarifying example that shows boundary case.
- Anchor that is too long pushes useful exemplars out of token window; keep anchor <= 2 sentences.
- For token-constrained clients (<=256 tokens), compress examples to single-line pairs; include 1 multi-line clarifying example.

Open questions:
- When is it better to accept "unknown" than risk hallucinated tag? (product decision: allow human review threshold?)
- Does including negative examples help across models or only smaller ones? early signs: helps rwd-3b, neutral for 13b. Need more runs.
- How to automatically surface new abbreviations from streaming input to seed exemplar updates? (idea: light-weight clustering + auto-suggest candidate new exemplar)

TODOs (fast):
- [ ] Spin up batch runs for experiment matrix; script seeds + deterministic RNG. Assign: Marcus (this week).
- [ ] Prototype post-filter mapper and integrate into evaluation harness. Priya.
- [ ] Draft short one-pager for product on tradeoff: unknown vs hallucination with examples.

Random notes / snippets:
- "anchor pattern" = short canonical mapping table at top. Works best when rules are few and deterministic.
- Keep a library of compressed exemplars for token-budget targets: compress_examples_v1.md (create).

Links/refs: JIRA INF-4321 (tracking runs), confluence FS-robustness-testplan, slack #prompt-lab thread: "abbrev-drift-jan24"

End of scratchpad. Will iterate; this doc is intentionally messy so I can copy bits into a PR or confluence later.
